_comment: Shared cross-language vectors for entity types with NO representation in the target schema (#7742, D3 fail closed). Both converters run every case: Rust rust/export/tests/schema_unrepresented_parity.rs (convert_step_line) and TypeScript packages/export/src/schema-unrepresented.parity.test.ts (convertStepLine). `refuses` means the converter must refuse the record (Rust Err, TS throw); otherwise `expect` is the converted line with the exact IFCPROXY GlobalId and Name (#11322). Rule: a record whose type the TARGET registry does not declare is refused unless it is an IfcRoot subtype (then an IFCPROXY), when the target is IFC2X3, or the target is IFC4 and the SOURCE is an IFC4X3 or an IFC2X3 that declares it (an IFC2X3 one neither on the verbatim list nor a varying action). IFC5 has no registry on either side. Scope: an IFC2X3 target refuses for every source as before; an IFC4 target checks an IFC4X3 source (#7742) and an IFC2X3 source (#10902), whose IFC2X3-only types are proxied when rooted, except the `routes` verbatim list (D59: non-rooted ones, refusing them failed real files) and the types another pass converts (`handled`: varying actions, which the structural pass reports, #9668; IfcPresentationStyleAssignment on an IFC4X3 target, which style flattening carries, D57). An IFC4X3 target is not checked yet (#10971). `routes` is the registry check's partition of every source-only type per pair: TypeScript schema-representation-registry.test.ts derives it from the tables, Rust checks each name's route.
